title: Chapter 126: A Brave Idea
html:
When Chen Ge left the previous day, the heads’ paint had still been wet, and the unfinished pieces had looked far less frightening. Once the workshop was open, he and the owner approached the counter.

“Look at this craftsmanship… Using your talent only for a Haunted House is such a waste.” The owner followed behind him and lifted a schoolgirl’s head from the table.

Once his initial fear faded, the bodiless heads began to fascinate him. They looked astonishingly human; emotion seemed to live in the girl’s eyes, replacing a mannequin’s usual emptiness.

“You really are the best dollmaker I’ve ever seen.” The owner studied the girl’s face for a full minute before reluctantly looking away. After some hesitation, he returned the head to its place and tapped the busy Chen Ge on the shoulder. “Brother, I came early because I wanted to discuss something with you.”

Brother?The sudden warmth and familiar address put Chen Ge on guard.

“Tell me, if I can help, I will.” Chen Ge was working on the design of the mannequin body.

“A deal that would benefit us both.” The owner handed him a business card. “We should stay in touch.”

“Qian Guigen?” Chen Ge wondered what had prompted the sudden friendliness. Once he accepted the card, Boss Qian lowered his voice. “I mainly design mannequins for stores and amusement parks, but advances in technology—especially 3D imaging—have reduced demand. I’ve considered moving into another field to keep the workshop afloat, but this industry is rigid. A drastic change would be difficult.”

“Every field is difficult. You should probably stick with what you know rather than risk losing your capital.” Chen Ge shaped a student’s body from clay, smoothing it with a damp sponge. Under the precise pressure of his fingers, the surface took on the sheen and texture of living skin. He paid little attention to Boss Qian; he wanted only to finish and transport the mannequins to the Haunted House.

“That’s what I thought before I met you. Then you showed me a ray of light through the fog—a brilliant new direction.” Boss Qian gazed at the expressive mannequin heads. “I have a bold idea!”

“Mind getting me the 16th carving knife?”

“Will you pay attention? If this succeeds, we could earn more in a month than your Haunted House makes in a year!” Boss Qian slapped both palms onto the table and stared at him.

The mention of money made Chen Ge pause. “Money doesn’t sway me, but I’m willing to hear your idea.”

“Small dolls sell cheaply, and the market for ordinary mannequins is dying. We should enter the luxury custom market!” Boss Qian carefully lifted one of the heads. “I’ve never seen anything this lifelike, and you used inferior materials. With premium materials, could you make a mannequin indistinguishable from a real person?”

“In theory,” Chen Ge replied, omitting that with the right materials, he could create an actual living doll.

“That talent is our road to riches!” Boss Qian pulled up several product photos on his phone. “Even these crudely made adult dolls sell online for more than eight thousand yuan. If we offer life-sized custom models with flawless skin and features, we can charge five figures. I’ve researched it—the market is wide open and will remain so for years.”

“Well, your idea definitely is brave.” Chen Ge shook his head and continued to focus on his clay body.

“Imagine the profit! At your speed, we could make twenty in three days—two hundred a month. Nothing on the market matches your quality, so we can start at fifteen thousand yuan apiece. Even with the best materials, that leaves ten thousand in profit per doll. Two million a month! Why cling to the Haunted House?” Boss Qian had expected far more enthusiasm.

“I won’t do anything illegal. Reproducing real people from photographs could violate their privacy.” Chen Ge was using the Dollmaker’s Talent, and its hidden dangers were unknown. He did not want to awaken to a headline announcing that a sex doll had killed its owner.

“Why are you so stubborn?” Boss Qian launched into his pitch. “Everyone is an island. Even married couples argue, but dolls never do. Given the chance, many people would choose to spend their lives with one. A person grows tired when you unload all your troubles on them; a doll won’t. We’d hurt no one. We’d give lonely souls a safe harbor in this world.”

“You’re in the wrong business. You should sell insurance.” Chen Ge returned to the clay body. The world was not as innocent as Boss Qian made it sound. If these mannequins entered mass production, the consequences could spiral out of control, and Chen Ge would share the blame.

“A bold idea deserves a chance! Make two samples today, and I’ll promote them. If no one bites, we’ll forget the whole thing.” The reference photos already on Boss Qian’s phone proved he had come prepared.

“Boss Qian, have you considered this situation? You’re in bed with a doll, but after you fall asleep, the doll slowly opens its eyes.”

“Why would a doll open its eyes?”

“If you don’t believe me, visit my Haunted House and experience them yourself. My mannequins differ from ordinary ones in more than appearance.” Chen Ge did not elaborate. Boss Qian seemed like a decent man, merely overenthusiastic.

Boss Qian looked at the heads on the counter and shivered, but refused to surrender. “Call me when you’ve reconsidered.”

Chen Ge finished the clay body and repeated the steps from yesterday.

At 9:00 a.m., Chen Ge packed the heads into three large cardboard boxes and hired a taxi to take them to New Century Park.

The bodies will be ready tonight. Tomorrow morning, Mu Yang High School can officially open to visitors.
